pregnancyData.summary: In the 180 registered trials found, about 88% of sampled trials listed pregnancy as an exclusion; 2 trials were found that studied pregnancy.
pregnancyData.labelNote: See the official label's pregnancy section for current wording.

breastfeedingData.summary: No lactation information found in the label data we hold.

sexSpecificData.summary: About 38% of participants in trials with posted results were women. Sex-specific dosing information exists.
sexSpecificData.dosingNote: FDA lowered the recommended starting dose for women in 2013 after evidence of higher next-morning blood levels.

GET_drug_pill.name: levonorgestrel and ethinylestradiol
GET_drug_pill.scoreNote: This score reflects how much evidence exists for women. It is not a safety rating.

pregnancyData.summary: In the 380 registered trials found, about 70% of sampled trials listed pregnancy as an exclusion; 0 trials were found that studied pregnancy.
pregnancyData.labelNote: Not used in pregnancy; contraceptive use is the intended purpose. Check the label for use while breastfeeding.

sexSpecificData.summary: About 100% of participants in trials with posted results were women. No sex-specific dosing information found.

alternatives.reliability_note: CDC lists 0.1-0.4% typical-use failure; verify exact figure.
alternatives.mood_evidence: In the large Danish cohort, hormonal methods incl. the hormonal IUD were associated with later antidepressant use; this is an association, absolute risk is small, and response varies.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Often greatly reduces bleeding. Needs a clinician to insert; spotting is common early on.

alternatives.mood_evidence: Progestin-only; mood evidence is mixed and limited. Individual response varies.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Bleeding pattern can be unpredictable. Needs a clinician to insert and remove.

alternatives.mood_evidence: Non-hormonal, so no direct hormonal mood mechanism. Direct mood studies are limited.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Can make periods heavier or more painful, especially at first. Needs a clinician to insert.

flags.wording: Low mood is a reported side effect of levonorgestrel and ethinylestradiol (it appears in the product label data). Sex comparison is not informative because almost all reports for this medicine are from women. Discuss with your doctor.
flags.alsoConsider: Symptoms can also have causes unrelated to medicines. See the Symptoms tab for conditions that can present this way.

flags.wording: Unusual tiredness / fatigue appears in voluntary adverse-event reports for levonorgestrel and ethinylestradiol, but we did not find it in the label data we hold. Reports cannot show cause. Discuss with your doctor if it bothers you.
flags.alsoConsider: Symptoms can also have causes unrelated to medicines. See the Symptoms tab for conditions that can present this way.

limitations: Adverse-event reports are voluntary and unverified; they cannot prove a medicine caused a symptom or show how often it happens.
Decision support only. Never stop a prescribed medicine without talking to your doctor.

methods.mood_evidence: Associated with later antidepressant use and depression diagnoses in a Danish cohort of >1M women, especially in adolescents (association, small absolute risk). Many women notice no change, so personal tracking matters.
methods.tradeoffs: Needs daily adherence. Small increase in clot risk; not suitable for everyone (e.g. migraine with aura). Often reduces cramps, acne and bleeding.

methods.mood_evidence: Evidence on mood is limited and mixed.
methods.tradeoffs: Needs very regular timing; irregular bleeding is common. Suitable when oestrogen is not.

methods.mood_evidence: No hormonal effect; no mood link expected.
methods.tradeoffs: Lower typical-use reliability than long-acting methods; protects against STIs.

methods.mood_evidence: Associated with mood changes in some observational data; evidence mixed.
methods.tradeoffs: Return of fertility can be delayed; long-term use is linked to reduced bone density.

methods.reliability_note: CDC range is wide by method; verify.
methods.tradeoffs: Typical-use failure varies widely (roughly 2-23% depending on method); needs consistent tracking and training.

accuracyNotes: The combined pill raises TOTAL cortisol mainly via binding proteins; FREE cortisol is usually not elevated. Do not describe it as raising 'stress hormones'.
Mood effects of hormonal contraception are an association in observational data; absolute risk is small and individual response varies.
